passage: Sumit, you say a man in a crisp uniform and a lanyard came to your flat asking to check the meter and for your card details? Hear what happened to me. I'm Mridul. At twenty-five a man in a khaki shirt and a badge rang my bell and said he was from the power company and needed my bill and an OTP to "fix an error." The uniform looked right and my first thought was to trust him. But something nagged me: a real officer wouldn't need an OTP. I said, "Please wait, I'll call the power company's number from my bill." He said he'd come back later and left quickly. The helpline confirmed no visit was planned. Anyone can buy a shirt and print a badge. Check through the official number, not the one they give you.

qa.q: What did the man ask Mridul for besides checking the meter?
What was Mridul thinking when the man asked for an OTP?
qa.a: Something nagged at Mridul, since a real officer wouldn't need an OTP, even though the uniform looked right and Mridul's first thought was to trust it.
Sumit should not share details, check through the official number on the bill or website, and tell a trusted person.

qa.q: How might the man have reacted to Mridul's plan to call?
qa.a: He left quickly, which suggests he did not want the check, though that is not proof.

grounding: A uniform and badge signal a role, but identity must be verified through the official channel because anyone can wear a costume.

passage: Rain was pouring and the lobby was closing in ten minutes when a man in a delivery uniform and a lanyard hurried to Tanvir's security desk. "Urgent parcel for the sixth floor, Damini Rao. I have to hand it to her myself," he said, dripping. The uniform looked right and the man looked tired, and Tanvir felt a pull to wave him through. Instead he said, "Sorry, I'll call her first." He dialled Damini's extension. "A parcel?" she said. "I didn't order anything. Don't send him up; I'll come down." The man said, "Never mind, wrong address," and walked back into the rain. Tanvir didn't know whether the man had been a scammer or just mistaken. He wrote the time and description in the visitor log.

qa.q: What did Tanvir do first at the desk?
qa.a: He said he would call Damini first, then dialled her extension.

qa.q: What was Tanvir feeling when he saw the man in the delivery uniform?
qa.a: He felt a pull to wave him through, out of sympathy for a tired, wet man, but he still chose to check.

qa.q: Why was calling Damini a good step?
qa.a: It verified the claim through a proper channel, since anyone can wear a uniform.

qa.q: How might the delivery man have felt when he was refused?
qa.a: Perhaps frustrated or embarrassed, or simply mistaken; Tanvir could not tell.

grounding: A young professional reads a uniform and lanyard as a signal of role but verifies through the proper channel despite time pressure and bad weather.
